question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream. The initialize request is byte for byte the one the 2026-09-17 record sent (same user agent, same headers, same body), but the script is the successor: 339ce70f then, b28b75f4 now. The successor adds a tools/list step after a 200 and a second well-known fallback; neither touches this request.

headers.www-authenticate: Bearer realm="OAuth", resource_metadata="https://mcp.notion.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", error="invalid_token", error_description="Missing or invalid access token"

decoded.challenge-unchanged: the challenge is byte for byte what the 2026-09-17 record observed: the same four parameters in the same order. The two runs used different versions of the prober's script, which differ only in steps taken after this request.
decoded.body: a JSON object repeating the error invalid_token and the same description
decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200; resource https://mcp.notion.com/mcp; resource_name Notion MCP (Beta); authorization_servers https://mcp.notion.com; scopes_supported: default (one scope); bearer_methods_supported: header. Unchanged since 09-17, including the Beta in the resource name
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200; registration_endpoint /register; scopes_supported default; code_challenge_methods_supported plain and S256, with plain still advertised; grants authorization_code, refresh_token, jwt-bearer; token auth client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none; id-jag grant profile; client_id_metadata_document_supported true; an introspection_endpoint. Unchanged since 09-17
decoded.not-measured: what the server does with a credential, and whether a client that offers the plain PKCE method is actually allowed to complete a flow with it

finding: Six days after the 2026-09-17 probe, the same initialize request came back identical in every field compared: the same 401, the same challenge with error invalid_token and its description, the same single scope named default, the same resource_name Notion MCP (Beta), and an authorization server that still advertises the plain PKCE method beside S256. Nothing moved, which is the whole of this record. The instrument is not identical and the comparison is limited accordingly: the 09-17 run used probe-mcp-339ce70f.sh and this one its successor probe-mcp-b28b75f4.sh, which adds a tools/list step after a 200 and a second well-known fallback. The initialize request, its headers and its user agent are unchanged between them, and those are what this record compares. The entry's noAccountNeeded cell stays false. The plain method staying on offer is worth re-recording rather than assuming: it is the weaker of the two and a client is free to choose it.
